rv.q: Yet, haunting as Shepard’s play is, a faint air of portentous reverence overhangs Scott Elliott’s production.
The evening is still a fulfilling encounter with great actors and a twisted and twisting vision of America's underclass.
Buried Child is as strange as it always was but it is no longer as spooky and as thrilling and certainly not as hilarious as I remember it in the Gary Sinese production.
